newsitem.title: UK: Instant view - UK NAO report on public finances.
newsitem.headline: Instant view - UK NAO report on public finances.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' reactions to the report from the UK's National Audit Office on the government's new economic assumptions underlying the public finances.
NEIL PARKER, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND (RFTV)

"I think in general it's a fairly reasonable set of assumptions. We always thought that the GDP forecast of underlying 2.5 percent was a bit on the high side and the idea of the PSBR for 97/98 to be revised up 500 million pounds is not unreasonable. I would not say it is a significantly large amount either."

"The report's not entirely clear. The market's in a state of confusion. The size of the revisions are modest and I don't really think it makes much difference." "I think cutting the estimates of savings from spend to save programme is dubious. You take it or leave it. And the underlying rate of growth in the economy is higher than 2.25. We currently have 3.5 percent growth and no inflation, so I find the downward revision rather odd."
